items.title: NAVIN XP name everywhere: system name, text console, installer, boot menu (NAVIN XP 3.0)
No Debian licence text on the text console - one NAVIN XP line instead
items.check: - Your PC. Your OS. Your Freedom.

items.title: New NAVIN XP boot splash: logo fades in with a breathing blue glow on a blue background
Circular loading indicator (24 frames) and 'Starting NAVIN XP...' text
Fixed: the NAVIN splash was always replaced by Debian's spinner - NAVIN XP theme is now the default
Boot splash shows what the kernel really found: CPU, RAM, graphics, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, audio, touchpad
Real boot progress line (systemd) and messages under the spinner, disk-unlock password prompt
Boot menu: Live Mode (default), Install NAVIN XP, Safe Graphics, Recovery Mode, Restart, Shutdown
items.check: RECOVERY, RESTART, SHUTDOWN = "Recovery Mode - NAVIN XP", "Restart", "Shutdown"

items.title: 15-second countdown (UEFI and legacy BIOS), arrow keys + Enter, Esc/c opens the GRUB command line
Dark-blue NAVIN XP boot menu theme with large rows
Recovery Mode opens the NAVIN Recovery page with safe graphics
Fixed 2.2.1 stop at the tty1 text screen: display guard tries safer graphics drivers until the desktop starts
Driver order: Intel SNA -> modesetting -> modesetting without acceleration -> fbdev -> VESA (BIOS)
Safe Graphics / Recovery boots use a safe driver from the start (only for that boot)
Graphical desktop is the default boot target
Text screen explains what happened and how to fix it when the desktop cannot start
items.check: the desktop could not start with any graphics driver

items.title: Installer named NAVIN XP 3.0 with the NAVIN XP logo and dark-blue sidebar
NAVIN XP Update Center: system, security, kernel, driver, Flatpak and NAVIN release updates
Real progress from APT's own status numbers (download + install), no invented percentages
Security-only updates (packages from Debian's -security suite)
Never removes packages: uses 'upgrade --with-new-pkgs', never dist-upgrade
Asks first before major updates (kernel, desktop core, 40+ packages) and makes a Timeshift snapshot when set up
Shutdown and sleep are blocked while packages install
items.check: "--why=Installing updates - please do not switch off"

items.title: Checks free disk space, internet, a running installation and battery before installing
Signature, checksum, dependency, lock and space errors explained in plain words
Update history from the APT log, plus a full log file
Pending restart detection (Debian flag or a newer kernel)
Download only + pause; resume continues APT's partial downloads
Low bandwidth mode (APT download speed limit)
Automatic mode: manual, notify daily, or install security updates daily (only on the charger)
Success shown only after a fresh check of what is still upgradable
Changelog of a package (double-click a row)
Password asked through the system (polkit action org.navin.update)
